root: The external cosine scores may be weak or semantically uncalibrated between final text hidden states and raw visual targets. Normalizing them to unit history weight would then inject an obligatory noisy history component while calling it relevance. ILVR's query-to-candidate cosine does not establish this per-text scoring premise.
first_nail: Before a costly training run, use a small fixed set of real multi-block samples and the same frozen ILVR-conditioned Teacher to compare uniform-history, cosine-history and shuffled-history metrics: record score entropy/contrast and selected candidate overlap, then a paired fixed-prefix next-text loss comparison if needed. If cosine is effectively uniform in both scores and target choices, or indistinguishable from shuffled history on that discriminating readout, the relevance premise has no supporting evidence. This model/probe work needs separate explicit authorization and is not run by the design review; a small inconclusive result is not a pass.
